introduction.system_description:
This is My Table-Top RPG called Reclaim the Realm (RtR) it is a d20 ruleset that focues primarily on Combat and Exploration. It is set in a Fantasy world that has a technological and culural development that can be compared to the renaissance era.
In this system each player controls a character that can perform various abilities depending on the chosen class and selected abilities. This character gets stronger as they adventure at which point they unlock more abilities, improve existing ones and get more powerful in general. The system's rules are mainly designed to support combat and exploration.
introduction.keywords_description: During this document you will find Keywords which are bold and underlined, example: [D20 TEST]. These Keywords are here to clearly indicate that the text is refering to a game machenic or how precisly it can interact with other mechanics.
introduction.d20_test_description: The core mechanic for which uncertanties are resolved is the [D20 TEST]. A [D20 TEST] requires the acting individual (usually the player) to roll a d20 and add a bonus to the result which is stated by the relveant ability. This result is then compared to a Difficulty Threshold ([DT]). If the resolt meets or exceeds the [DT] the result is a success. Additionally if the d20 die rolled is a 20 the result is a critical success, if the die shows a 1, it is a critical failure. What impact these reults have is stated in the relevant ability/mechanic.
introduction.d20_test_specializations_description: There are various specific [D20 TEST] that have their own keywords to simplify the text. Some examples include [MARTIAL TEST], [SPELL TEST], [STABILITY TEST], [DODGE TEST], [TOUGHNESS TEST], [WILLPOWER TEST]. The specefic of which will be explained later on.
introduction.difficulty_threshold_description: The difficulty of any [D20 TEST] is measured by the Difficulty Threshld ([DT]). The [DT] should be exlusivly based upon the difficulty of the action the actor attempts. Below are examples on what the [DT] number translates to in difficulty. It should be kept in mind that different forms of a [D20 TEST] can achieve significantly higher bonuses.
introduction.difficulty_threshold_5: Trivial task for an avarage person
introduction.difficulty_threshold_10: Challenging task for an avarage person
introduction.difficulty_threshold_15: Difficult task for an avarage person
introduction.difficulty_threshold_20: Difficult task for a trained person in that task
introduction.difficulty_threshold_25: Difficult task for an expert in that task
introduction.difficulty_threshold_30: Difficult task for a genius in that task
introduction.difficulty_threshold_35: Impossible task for almost all mortal person
introduction.advantage_disadvantage:
There are 2 common ways to modify a [D20 TEST], the first one is to just add or subtract a flat number to the test or set the [DT] higher or lower. The second one is to grant advantage/disadvantage.
[ADVANTAGE]: You roll the d20 twice and take the better result.
[DISADVANTAGE]: You roll the d20 twice and take the worse result.
You can only benefit from one instance of [ADVANTAGE] or [DISADVANTAGE] at a time and if a [D20 TEST] has both, they cancel each other out.
introduction.abilitiies_description:
Every mechanical action performed by a charceter or npc is an ability. Each Ability specificies relevant characteristics such as range, target(s), and usage cost. Additionally it describes how the ability works and what it does.
The Ability also contains Tags which are indicators and later used to indicate what abilities can interact with other abilities.

character.creation_description: The Collapse of the Ancient World has left civilizations ravaged and isolated and the wilderness more dangerous than ever. Your Character will have to be strong, fast or cunning to survive out there and explore the remains. Use the following procedure to create your character:
character.creation_step_assign_attributes_skills: Assign your starting Attributes and Skills
character.creation_step_choose_perks_abilities: Pick your starting Perks and Abilities
character.species_description: Your species represents your biological make and your ancestry. Species also have certain traits that make them unique to others.
character.species_human_decription: Humans are the unique since they only started to emerge during the unification of the elemental planes in the material plane and did not form during or before the elemental turmoil. They are a very communal species and require social interaction in their lives. They are the most versatile of all people and also have a strong drive to make a name for themselves and achieve something in their lives.
character.species_dwarf_description: Dwarves originally formed in the Elemental Plane of Earth as an evolution of advanced earth elementals. A sizeable amount of dwarves still remain there, however most of them migrated to the Material Plane eventually. Their connections still remain strong and they mostly reside in mountanous regions where the connection the their native plane is the strongest. They have a very strict society and strongly adhere to the codes of their clan or society. Thus they are very suspecious of people outside their communities, however once you earn they trust they will welcome you as their own.
character.species_elf_description: Elves originate form the Elemental Plane of Air after evolving from the advanced AIr Elementals. Their ability to live there was limited since they are not able to fly innatly and thus most of them migrated towards the Material Plane when it formed. They are remarkable for their slender and tall physique and are the first people to master the ethereal plane and have built a strong connection. Which has evolved them to the point everytime a new elf is born instead of creating a new soul, a soul of a previous dead elf inhabits them and merges with their.
character.origin_description: Your origin defines the place you grew up and your early childhood, while this also slightly impacts your character’s abilities and skills, most importantly, it adds a lot of flavour and depth to your character. In the following steps you are presented with tables which you can roll, this however is optional. It merely represents the likelihood of where people are usually born, and can of course also be chosen freely.
character.birthplace_description: This table represents the location of your birth and where you spent most of your childhood. Depending on what you select, this affects your choices later on, so be aware that certain options might not be available to you later on. When you have chosen your Location, you can roll on the Family Table according to your Location.
character.early_training_description:
This represents what training or tutelage you recieved during adolescence which is usually heavily influenced by your parents. You gain [ADVANTAGE] on any [CHA] [ATTRIBUTE TEST] when interacting with persons of the same profession or background. This step also grants you extra an extra class skills, extra starting coins, and other bonuses.
If this skill is also a class skill for your chosen class you can instead choose a different one.
character.life_events_description: You can choose up to 3 Life Events that happened to your character. There are multiple Tables to choose from and you can choose multiple memories from the same table but you can’t choose the same life event multiple times.
character.adventuring_goal:
When creating your character you should pick one Adventuring Goal which should be the defining personal Goal and adventuring Motivation that you are persuing on the side. When creating your goal work with the GM to ensure you are both on the same page.
However keep in mind that you are usually working in an adventuring group so you will have to be aligned with the rest of the party for persuing your goal. Below you find some example Goals that you can use and adapt:
character.achieving_adventuring_goal: Upon Completion of your Adventuring Goal. You gain an extra Fate point. TODO add link to Fate
character.class_description:
Each player character must choose from one of the following classes below. The Class determines the core set of abilities your character is able to use out- but especially in-combat. When your character reaches a higher [LEVEL], their abilities become stronger and they will gain newer ones. Your class will later also allow you to specialize in different ways. After having chosen your class, you have to make choices for skills and certain abilities your class possesses, such as spells.
Below are summaries for each Class which show you the key characteristics of each class which are explained below:
character.class_hp_per_level: Represents your Class Bonus for determining your [HP] increase each [LEVEL].
character.class_martial_level_progression: Determines the factor with which your [MARTIAL LEVEL] increases with your [LEVEL]. The higher the value the better your character is at fighting using their martial prowess, superior tactics, or charismatic leadership.
character.class_spell_level_progression: Determines the factor with which your [SPELL LEVEL] increases with your [LEVEL]. The higher the value, the better your character is at casting spells. A value of 0 indicates no spellcasting ability.
character.class_defenses: The Factor with which your Defense Values increase with each [LEVEL]. These are relevant when attempting to resist or evade incoming dangers
character.class_class_attributes: Each class has 3 Class Attributes, which are relevant for the classes most important abilities. Additionally these abilities have a higher attribute limit and are each increased by 2 when selecting the class.
character.class_skills: Your class skills, these skills have their rank and rank limit increased by 2.
character.class_perks_description: Each Class also has a specific set of Perks which are imporvements towards your character that you can pick and choose to best fit your Chracter. Which will be explained in more detail.TODO add link to Perks
